name: Stuttgart Airport
before:
Stuttgart's airport, about 13 km south of the city, and sixth busiest in Germany with 11,832,634 passengers in 2018.

The terminal layout sounds more complicated than it is. There are four passenger terminals with separate check-in areas and entrances, but they are directly connected to each other and share a single airside area, so once a client is through security the building is one space. The catch is boarding: that shared airside has only eight jet bridges against roughly two dozen bus-boarding stands, so expect a bus to the aircraft more often than not.

Terminal 1, with Terminal 1-West, has 50 check-in counters and is mainly Eurowings and Turkish Airlines. Terminal 2 is small, nine counters inside the shopping area.

The Messe Stuttgart exhibition centre, the ninth largest in Germany, moved to grounds directly next to the airport in 2007, which makes this a genuinely convenient arrival for a trade fair.

It is named in honour of Manfred Rommel, a former mayor of Stuttgart.
after:
Stuttgart's airport, about 13 km south of the city. It handled 9.6 million passengers in 2025.

There are four passenger terminals and a single runway of 3,345 metres.

The Messe Stuttgart exhibition centre moved to grounds right by the airport in 2007, which makes this a convenient arrival for a trade fair.

It is named in honour of Manfred Rommel, a former Lord Mayor of Stuttgart.
